qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant global oligopoly (Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer, Oliver Wyman) protected by deep carrier integration, regulatory licensing across 130+ countries, proprietary loss analytics, and >95% client retention. Collects an ad-valorem toll on rising commercial insurance premiums with near-zero balance sheet underwriting risk. Empirical proof: 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 17.0%, tangible ROIC >100%, and consistent 15+ year operating margin expansion (EBIT margin >23%). Primary erosion threats: aggressive broker poaching, regulatory scrutiny of contingent commissions, and potential soft-market premium rate declines.

qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle track record shows revenue expanding from $13.2B in 2016 to $27.0B in 2025, with GAAP EBIT compounding from $2.4B to $6.2B and Owner EPS growing from $3.73 to $9.67 without a single peak-to-peak breakdown. 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 16.95% (ranging 12.6% to 19.8% despite large goodwill balances from JLT and McGriff acquisitions). Balance sheet safely absorbed the $7.75B cash acquisition of McGriff in late 2024: LT debt peaked at $19.4B and already decreased to $18.3B in 2025; cash stands at $2.69B, leaving Net Debt at $15.63B (3.39x Owner FCF, repayable within ~3.4 years). FY2025 EBIT of $6.22B covers interest expense ($960M) by 6.48x (>5.0x hurdle). Operating businesses (Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer, Oliver Wyman) maintain unmatched scale and client lock-in across global commercial risk transfer.
